submitted.rationale: Index 17 (In0.415Sb0.585) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0248%. EQE rose with Sb content across all three measurements: 0.0052% at Sb 0.22, 0.0174% at Sb 0.51 and 0.0248% at Sb 0.585. Index 17 lies between the InSbO4 phase (on the MACE hull, predicted gap 2.2 eV) and In3Sb5O12, so it may be a phase mixture. I did not use XRD, so the phase makeup of any sample is unconfirmed.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.0052%, the lowest of the three, even though In11Sb3O24 is stable with a predicted 1.9 eV gap.
Not measured because the budget ran out. The predicted In3Sb5O12 gap of 2.77 eV is above the 2.7 eV photon energy, so absorption may drop there, but the trend could also keep rising.

consultations.verdict: Support: In11Sb3O24 (Sb 0.214) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 1.91 eV < 2.7 eV photon energy, so it absorbs; index 6 (Sb 0.220) matches this stoichiometry. InSb3/5 phase gap 2.77 eV is likely non-absorbing.

Support: InSbO4 (Sb 0.5) is on the MACE hull and its MEGNet HSE gap is 2.2 eV (below 2.7 eV), so it can absorb the illumination. Index 15 (Sb 0.51) is the closest composition, which makes it a good test of the equimolar region after index 6 came back low.

Weak support. Sb oxides such as Sb2O4 have a predicted gap of 1.67 eV, so they absorb. Adding Sb beyond InSbO4 could keep the rising trend going (EQE went from 0.005 at index 6 to 0.017 at index 15). In3Sb5O12 (gap 2.77 eV, 0.018 eV/atom above hull) at higher Sb may not absorb, so index 17 (Sb 0.585) is a moderate step toward the Sb-rich side. It also sits in the GP top 5.
